prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” broker for every self‑employed person in Kansas City — the right broker depends on your age, household income (for ACA subsidies), whether you need family coverage, whether you want to see certain doctors, and whether you prefer an independent agent vs. a captive agent for a single carrier. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best broker for you and some vetted options to consider.

What to look for in a broker
- Independent agent (represents multiple carriers) so you get comparisons, not just one brand.  
- Experience with ACA/marketplace enrollments and subsidy rules.  
- Transparent fees and clear explanation of monthly premium vs. total out‑of‑pocket costs.  
- Good local reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and professional licensing (Missouri insurance license).  
- Willingness to do a side‑by‑side comparison, explain networks/formularies, and help with year‑round service (claims, renewals, midyear changes).  

Places to start searching
- HealthCare.gov: if you’re buying an individual plan in Missouri you use the federal marketplace; brokers/agencies can enroll you at no extra cost and help you determine subsidy eligibility.  
- National marketplaces/brokers that serve self‑employed people: eHealth and HealthSherpa both let you compare marketplace and off‑exchange plans online and will connect you with licensed agents. Stride (for freelancers) provides plan search tools and tax/subsidy guidance.  
- Local independent agencies: search “independent health insurance agent Kansas City” and filter by reviews and years in business. Look for agents who explicitly advertise ACA/help for the self‑employed or small business (SHOP) plans.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Do you represent multiple carriers? Which ones?  
- Do you charge a broker fee or is your help free for marketplace enrollments?  
- How will you compare out‑of‑pocket costs (deductible, copays, out‑of‑network)?  
- Will you help with renewals and claims year‑round?  
- Can you show side‑by‑side quotes for premiums, total expected annual cost, and provider network coverage?

Quick plan tips for self‑employed people
- If your household income is moderate, check eligibility for ACA premium tax credits — a broker can calculate this for you.  
- Silver plans can be best if you qualify for cost‑sharing reductions; otherwise look at premium vs deductible tradeoffs.  
- If you have employees or plan to hire, ask about SHOP/small‑group options.  
- Consider short‑term needs (dedicated doctor, meds) when comparing networks and formularies.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top‑rated licensed independent brokers or agencies near your ZIP code in Kansas City, MO; or  
- Compare example plan quotes if you tell me your age(s), ZIP code, household income, and whether you use tobacco or have specific doctors/medications to keep.

Which would you prefer?
